name: DashboardPage
description: One page of a dashboard: a title with its actions, a row of key numbers, then your content. It sits inside DashboardShell but works anywhere. The title is the page's h1.

title.description: The page's title, shown as its h1.

description.description: One or two sentences under the title.

actions.description: Buttons for the right of the title, e.g. Export and Add customer.

stats.description: The key numbers shown in a row of cards under the title: label, value, and optionally a trend, a small history and a note.

isLoading.description: Show the key numbers as skeletons and mark the page busy.

children.description: The rest of the page: charts, tables, forms.

keyboard: Tab: moves through the actions, then the page content
requirements: The title is the page's only h1, so there is one clear heading to jump to
The key numbers are a labelled section (heading "Key numbers", read only by screen readers) and each one reads as a sentence
Columns share the width equally, so a long number never pushes the others off screen; two columns on a phone, four on a wide screen
While loading the page is marked busy and numbers are skeletons, never made-up values
screenReader: "Key numbers" section, then "Monthly revenue: $48,200. Up 12% compared with last month."

use_when: The top of any page inside a dashboard
avoid_when: Pages with a long form as the main content: use a plain heading and the form
anti_patterns: More than one h1 on a page
Showing placeholder numbers while data loads

contract.data: A title, an optional description, and stats as plain objects.
